summary: Design how the Wave-S Job reducer becomes the block-intake engine so connect_tip/process_block_core become dead and the legacy engine deletes cleanly

traces.area: TRACE A — live block-ingest path (process_new_block → connect_tip) and the gap the Job reducer does not yet own
findings: ENTRY: lib/net/src/msg_blocks.c:324 process_block_msg deserializes the wire block, dedup-checks block_already_seen (:310), then calls process_new_block(&state, mp->main_state, mp->coins_tip, params, &blk, false, datadir) UNCONDITIONALLY (no cutover flag). On valid return it marks-seen + decays peer score (:340,:357-369); the reducer is NOT consulted on this path.

process_new_block (lib/validation/src/process_block_core.c:1012-1050) is a 3-step sequence: (1) check_block(:1022) PoW/merkle/tx structural check; (2) accept_block(:1030) header-admit + body disk-write; (3) activation_request_connect(boot_activation_controller(), ACTIVATION_SRC_NEW_BLOCK, pblock, &ao) at :1043 — it does NOT connect inline, it hands off to the activation controller. coins_tip is explicitly ignored (:1020 `(void)coins_tip`).

accept_block (lib/validation/src/accept_block.c:38-322) MUTATES in-mem block_index: calls accept_block_header (:47) which calls add_to_block_index (accept_block_header.c:531) → block_map_insert into ms->map_block_index, sets BLOCK_VALID_TREE; refreshes header/nHeight/nChainWork (:57-67); writes the block bytes to disk via find_block_pos+write_block_to_disk (:246-254); sets BLOCK_HAVE_DATA via block_index_set_have_data_verified (:267), promotes to BLOCK_VALID_TRANSACTIONS (:269), sets nTx/nChainTx (:271-273), and BFS-propagates nChainTx forward (:281-319). It does NOT touch coins.db or the active-chain tip.

activation_request_connect (app/services/src/chain_activation_controller.c:342-496) is the serialization gate: builds an activation_request, runs the pure planner activation_should_connect (:285), and under ctl->mutex (:382) calls activate_best_chain(&vs, ctl->ms, ctl->coins_tip, params, pblock, datadir) at :405, then drains deferred passes within a 2s budget (:420-444). This is the single live connect authority — NOT the reducer.

activate_best_chain (lib/validation/src/activate_best_chain.c, 46KB) selects the most-work chain via find_most_work_chain (process_block_core.c:290-427) and calls connect_tip per block to walk the active tip forward to the selected candidate. It is the ~20-caller hub the design wants dead.

connect_tip (lib/validation/src/connect_tip.c:90-990) is where the REAL connection happens. It: reads the block from disk if pblock==NULL (:148-250, with hash+merkle verify); builds a child coins_view over coins_tip (:259-277); calls connect_block (:284) — the full consensus engine (Equihash already done, but ECDSA scripts, Sapling/Sprout proofs, JoinSplit sigs, BIP30, update_coins UTXO mutation, Sapling tree update via connect_block_set_sapling_tree :282); flushes the coins_view into coins_tip (:523 coins_view_cache_flush); SETS THE TIP via update_tip(ms,pindex_new) at :616 → process_block_commit_tip → chain_evidence_controller_promote_tip or csr_commit_tip → chain_set_active_tip → active_chain_set_tip (the ONLY mutation of chain_active.chain[]); promotes pindex to BLOCK_VALID_SCRIPTS (:641); persists block_index to LevelDB sync (:702); forces at-tip coins.db commit (:718 flush_coins_if_needed true); writes tx_index (:738-771); syncs the WALLET (:779-820 wallet_sync_transaction + Sapling trial-decrypt + nullifier-spend); removes confirmed txs from MEMPOOL (:826-830 tx_mempool_remove_for_block); appends MMR/MMB leaves (:860,:870); periodic UTXO commitment (:957).

update_tip (process_block_core.c:840-910) is the tip-set funnel: process_block_commit_tip (:849) → chain_evidence_controller_promote_tip (:754) under node.db, else csr_commit_tip (:791). The ZCL_TESTING fallback at :801 is the only place active_chain_set_tip-equivalent chain_set_active_tip is called with TIP_FROM_CONNECT. update_tip then emits EV_TIP_UPDATED (:892).

chain_set_active_tip (app/services/src/chain_tip.c:106) is the production tip mutator; its live callers are ALL legacy/recovery: process_block_core.c:801,874 (connect/disconnect), msg_headers.c:609, snapshot_apply.c:299, block_index_integrity.c:562, utxo_recovery_service.c:89, chain_restore_executor.c:60, block_index_loader{,_rebuild}.c. NO reducer stage calls it. (grep confirms active_chain_set_tip itself appears only in lib/test/* — production goes through chain_set_active_tip.)

lib/validation/src/chainstate.c:248,266,338 active_chain_tip/at/height — already route through a registered authority (g_chain_authority) when is_authoritative() true (tip_finalize registers it, chainstate.c:223 + tip_finalize_stage.c:527)
lib/validation/src/accept_block_header.c:531 add_to_block_index — in-mem block_index producer (called from net msg_headers.c:364, header_probe.c, accept_block.c:47)
risks: MUTATIONS THE REDUCER ALREADY REPRODUCES (steps 1-9): (a) in-mem block_index creation+VALID_TREE: header_admit/accept path via add_to_block_index, and header_admit_stage.c:296 re-emits EV_BLOCK_HEADER; (b) BLOCK_HAVE_DATA + EV_BLOCK_HEADER re-emit: body_persist_stage.c:326-327 after disk read+hash+merkle verify; (c) script verification: script_validate_stage; (d) Sapling/Sprout/JoinSplit proof verification: proof_validate_stage.c:218-280 (real bn254/groth16 calls); (e) UTXO delta + projection authorship: utxo_apply_stage.c:260-261 emit_delta when UTXO_AUTHOR_STAGE; (f) per-block inverse-delta for reorg-unwind: utxo_apply_delta_persist :271; (g) tip-finalize record + finalized tip hash: tip_finalize_stage.c:471-480. Reads (gettxoutsetinfo, active_chain_height) already route through projection/authority.

THE GAP connect_tip STILL EXCLUSIVELY OWNS (NOT yet in the reducer): (1) ACTUAL TIP MUTATION — no stage calls active_chain_set_tip/chain_set_active_tip; the reducer only WRITES tip_finalize_log and registers an authority that REPORTS the tip, but the in-mem chain_active.chain[] array it reads is filled exclusively by legacy connect_tip→update_tip. tip_finalize_stage step_finalize itself reads active_chain_at(ms,next_h+1) for new_tip (tip_finalize_stage.c:404-405) — it is a passenger on legacy's tip advance, not the driver. (2) coins.db (coins_view_sqlite) write/flush — connect_tip.c:523,718 own the authoritative UTXO SQLite commit; utxo_apply only emits to the utxo_projection (still UTXO_AUTHOR_LEGACY by default per update_coins.c:53). (3) WALLET sync (connect_tip.c:779-820). (4) MEMPOOL eviction (connect_tip.c:826-830). (5) tx_index LevelDB write (connect_tip.c:738). (6) MMR/MMB append (connect_tip.c:860,870). (7) SHA3 UTXO checkpoint enforcement (connect_tip.c:544). (8) LevelDB block_index durable write (connect_tip.c:702).

CHICKEN-AND-EGG / KEYSTONE BLOCKER for making the reducer the engine: EVERY stage's step body keys off active_chain_at(&ms->chain_active, h) (header_admit_stage.c:270, body_persist_stage.c:267, utxo_apply_stage.c:224, tip_finalize_stage.c:404). That array is ONLY populated by active_chain_set_tip, which today is driven by legacy connect_tip. To make the reducer drive ingestion, header_admit/body_persist must first OWN block_index insertion (today via legacy add_to_block_index in the net/accept path) AND a stage must own active_chain_set_tip to extend the in-mem chain — neither exists yet. tip_finalize must transition from RECORDING the tip to SETTING it (call active_chain_set_tip / become the writer, not just the registered authority that reads back the legacy-filled array).

P2P/MINING/REORG entry points that must be re-pointed when connect_tip dies (process_new_block has ~6 live callers): msg_blocks.c:324, msg_compact.c, miner.c, mining_controller.c (submitblock), repair_controller_rebuild.c. These must enqueue into the reducer (e.g. header_admit_inbox + body source) instead of calling process_new_block; otherwise deleting connect_tip/activate_best_chain breaks block intake. Reorg today is handled by activate_best_chain disconnect/connect + disconnect_tip + chain_evidence promote_tip synthesizing rollback_auth (process_block_core.c:771); the reducer's reorg story is cursor-rewind (header_admit_stage.c:243, tip_finalize_stage.c:291 rewind_cursor_if_active_chain_reorged + utxo_apply reorg-unwind via inverse-delta) — these REACT to a reorg already applied to chain_active by legacy; they do not THEMSELVES disconnect/reconnect the in-mem tip.

DEFAULT AUTHORS ARE STILL LEGACY: cutover_modes gate header_admit_get_mode / tip_finalize_get_mode / utxo_projection_get_author — all default to SHADOW/UTXO_AUTHOR_LEGACY (update_coins.c:53, header_admit_stage.c:286, tip_finalize_stage.c:485 via cutover_modes). So today the stages run ALONGSIDE legacy as observers; flipping authors without first wiring tip-set + block_index ownership into the stages would leave the chain with no tip writer.

traces.area: TRACE B — the 8-stage Wave-S reducer pipeline as it runs today: what drives it, what feeds it, and its exact dependency on the legacy connect engine
findings: DRIVER: All 8 stages are driven by per-stage supervisor children in app/supervisors/src/staged_sync_supervisor.c (registered in pipeline order at staged_sync_supervisor_register, line 413-430). Each child ticks every period_secs=2 (e.g. line 79), and its on_tick drains a bounded batch then reports cursor as progress, e.g. header_admit_tick at staged_sync_supervisor.c:42-52 calls header_admit_stage_drain(HEADER_ADMIT_BATCH_PER_TICK=500) then supervisor_progress(id, header_admit_stage_cursor()). There is NO single drain loop; it is 8 independent supervised tickers in the g_chain_sup domain.

CURSOR: Progress is a per-stage cursor in progress.kv stage_cursor table. Each step reads cursor_in and on JOB_ADVANCED sets cursor_out = cursor_in + 1 (e.g. header_admit_stage.c:302, body_fetch_stage.c:214). Downstream stages floor against the upstream stage's DURABLY-persisted cursor via stage_cursor_persisted() in app/jobs/include/jobs/stage_helpers.h:35 (e.g. body_fetch floors on validate_headers at body_fetch_stage.c:158-163; utxo_apply floors on proof_validate at utxo_apply_stage.c:199-204; tip_finalize floors on utxo_apply at tip_finalize_stage.c:359-382). Reading the persisted (not in-mem) cursor decouples init order and gives natural backpressure.

WHAT FEEDS header_admit (the entry stage): It does NOT pull from the network or the log independently. step_admit (header_admit_stage.c:257-306) reads active_chain_at(&ms->chain_active, cursor_in) at line 270; if no block exists at that height it returns JOB_IDLE (line 271). So header_admit consumes the LIVE in-memory active chain that the legacy path has ALREADY populated. There is also a secondary mailbox feed: header_probe.c:75-89 (hp_publish_header_admit) pushes header_admit_msg, drained in header_admit_stage_step_once at header_admit_stage.c:382 (handle_header_admit_msg, line 93-123) — but that handler also only re-reads active_chain_at and logs; it creates nothing.

header_probe is the ONE genuine external puller, and it feeds the LEGACY indexer, not the stage: header_probe.c pulls headers from a running zclassicd via JSON-RPC (HP_DEFAULT_HOST 127.0.0.1, HP_DEFAULT_PORT 8232, header_probe.c:44-45) and calls the LEGACY accept_block_header(&hdr, &vs, ms, params, &pindex) at header_probe.c:182 and :201, which does add_to_block_index into ms->map_block_index (accept_block_header.c:531). It then posts to the header_admit inbox. So even the header inflow into the in-mem index is performed by the legacy function, not by any stage.

body_fetch does NOT fetch from peers — it only OBSERVES the legacy-set BLOCK_HAVE_DATA flag. step_body_fetch (body_fetch_stage.c:140-216) reads active_chain_at (line 178) and checks bi->nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_DATA (line 200); if the body is not on disk it returns JOB_IDLE without advancing (line 200-205). The in-code comment is explicit: 'The natural backpressure: cursor stays put until msg_blocks brings it in' (body_fetch_stage.c:203-204) and the header says 'no peer fetch triggered from this module. The live msg_blocks pipeline continues to drive actual body acquisition; S-4 watches' (body_fetch_stage.h:7-9).

All body-consuming middle stages read the body from DISK via the legacy-populated position, not from any independent store. stage_default_block_reader (stage_helpers.h:58-71) guards on BLOCK_HAVE_DATA and preads from bi->nFile / bi->nDataPos — fields set by the legacy accept_block.c:252 write_block_to_disk and connect_tip.c:156. Confirmed callers: body_persist_stage.c:267-277 (IDLE if !HAVE_DATA at :268), script_validate_stage.c:336-346, proof_validate_stage.c:418-428, utxo_apply_stage.c:224-234 (IDLE if !HAVE_DATA at :225).

TERMINAL STAGE tip_finalize is purely observational and CANNOT connect a tip. step_finalize (tip_finalize_stage.c:347-482) reads old_tip = active_chain_at(next_h) and new_tip = active_chain_at(next_h+1) (lines 404-406); if new_tip does not yet exist it returns JOB_IDLE (line 407-410). It never calls connect_tip/activate_best_chain/active_chain_set_tip; on success it merely writes a 'finalized' row to tip_finalize_log (line 471) and bumps the cursor. The active chain must ALREADY be advanced past next_h (by the legacy engine) before tip_finalize records anything.

CURRENT MODE = all SHADOW. cutover_modes default bitmask is 0 (app/services/src/cutover_modes.c:15 static _Atomic unsigned g_header_pipeline_modes = 0), and every *_get_mode returns SHADOW unless the corresponding bit is set (cutover_modes.c:71-92). So header_admit/validate_headers/tip_finalize report HEADER_ADMIT/..._MODE_SHADOW and utxo_apply emits to the projection only if utxo_projection_get_author()==UTXO_AUTHOR_STAGE (utxo_apply_stage.c:260), which is LEGACY by default (comment utxo_apply_stage.c:258-259).

Even AUTHORITATIVE mode does NOT make the stage the ingestion/connect engine. authoritative_admit (header_admit_stage.c:125-144) only promotes an EXISTING block_index's nStatus to BLOCK_VALID_TREE; it requires bi to already exist. The active_chain authority hook tip_finalize registers (active_chain_register_authority at tip_finalize_stage.c:521-527) only changes what active_chain_tip/_height/_at RETURN when is_authoritative() is true (chainstate.c:248-264, 328-336, 338-347) and set_tip_cb (tip_finalize_stage.c:502-508) only updates the stage's own last-advance tracker. The in-mem c->chain[] array is still physically populated solely by active_chain_set_tip (chainstate.c:279-336).

EXACT DEPENDENCY / ANSWER: The pipeline CANNOT connect a brand-new tip block end-to-end on its own right now. It depends entirely on the legacy connect engine having ALREADY run for that height. The legacy chain that the stages read off is built by: msg_blocks.c:324 process_new_block -> activate_best_chain -> connect_tip (writes body to disk + sets BLOCK_HAVE_DATA at connect_tip.c:156 / accept_block.c:252; runs connect_block/update_coins) -> process_block_core.c (chain_state_repository commit path) -> chain_state_repository.c:702 active_chain_set_tip -> populates ms->chain_active.chain[]. ONLY THEN can header_admit/body_fetch/.../tip_finalize observe and log that height. The reducer mirrors; it does not drive.

risks: To make the reducer the actual intake/connect engine, header_admit (or a new ingestion seam) must be given a real header source that does NOT route through legacy accept_block_header. Today header_probe is the only puller and it calls the legacy add_to_block_index; P2P headers/blocks arrive via msg_blocks/msg_headers into process_new_block. There is currently no stage-owned path that inserts into map_block_index or allocates a block_index from a raw wire header.

active_chain_set_tip (the in-mem chain[] populator) is called only by the legacy wrappers (chain_tip.c / chain_state_repository.c) driven from process_block_core/activate_best_chain — NOT by any stage. Every stage from header_admit through tip_finalize reads active_chain_at and returns JOB_IDLE when the height is absent, so deleting connect_tip/activate_best_chain without first relocating active_chain_set_tip population into the stage path would freeze the entire pipeline at the current tip.

Body acquisition is entirely legacy: body_fetch is observe-only and write_block_to_disk + BLOCK_HAVE_DATA are set inside accept_block.c/connect_tip.c. Making the reducer authoritative requires a stage that actually requests bodies from peers and writes them to disk, which does not exist in app/jobs today.

AUTHORITATIVE mode (cutover) only redirects active_chain accessor RETURNS to the stage tip and lets utxo_apply author the projection — it does not move ingestion/connection into the stages. Flipping modes alone will leave the pipeline still dependent on legacy to physically populate chain[] and disk, so 'delete legacy connect' is not unblocked by the cutover bits as currently wired.

tip_finalize's reorg handling is detection-only (logs 'reorg_detected' at tip_finalize_stage.c:419-430 and rewinds its own cursor); the actual disconnect/reorg unwind of the active chain is still performed by legacy disconnect_tip/activate_best_chain. A stage-driven engine must own reorg unwind (disconnect + UTXO inverse-delta apply) before connect_tip/disconnect_tip can be deleted without breaking reorg.

header_probe points at 127.0.0.1:8232 (a separate running zclassicd oracle); if the reducer is to ingest independently, the design must replace this RPC-from-oracle header source with a true P2P/log-driven source, or the node remains coupled to an external zclassicd.

traces.area: TRACE C — the live callers of process_new_block / connect_tip / activate_best_chain / accept_block: repoint map for making the Job reducer the actual intake/connect engine
findings: GROUND TRUTH — the '26 callers' is mostly comments/decls. The ACTUAL non-test CALL SITES are far fewer. process_new_block(): exactly 5 call sites — lib/net/src/msg_blocks.c:324 (P2P full block), lib/net/src/msg_compact.c:60 (compact block reassembled), lib/mining/src/miner.c:224 (process_block_found, mined block), app/controllers/src/mining_controller.c:196 (submitblock RPC), app/controllers/src/repair_controller_rebuild.c:179 (rebuild_recent recovery). activate_best_chain(): exactly 2 call sites, BOTH inside the controller drain loop — app/services/src/chain_activation_controller.c:405 and :437. accept_block(): exactly 1 call site — process_block_core.c:1030 (inside process_new_block). connect_tip()/disconnect_tip(): only called from inside activate_best_chain.c (12 sites) and process_block_invalidate.c:229 / process_block_self_heal.c:695. So connect_tip/disconnect_tip have ZERO external callers — they are private to the activate loop + invalidate/self-heal.

THE REAL FAN-IN IS activation_request_connect() (the controller is already the single connect serializer). 9 non-test callers: process_block_core.c:1043 (ACTIVATION_SRC_NEW_BLOCK — the tail of process_new_block), config/src/boot.c:3230 (ACTIVATION_SRC_BOOT), config/src/boot_services.c:1898 (boot), lib/net/src/msg_headers.c:647/706/722 (ACTIVATION_SRC_BLOCK_FILE_SCAN / HEADERS_ALL_DATA — all-data-present trigger), app/services/src/sync_monitor.c:168, app/conditions/src/utxo_activation_paused.c:77, app/services/src/chain_activation_controller.c:181 (internal kick), app/controllers/src/repair_controller.c:239, process_block_revalidate.c:384 + process_block_invalidate.c:317/380 (reconsider/invalidate reconnect). EVERY connect ultimately funnels through chain_activation_controller.c:342 activation_request_connect -> mutex -> activate_best_chain. This is the existing single chokepoint; the reducer must REPLACE the body of that chokepoint, not 26 scattered sites.

GROUP 1 — APPLY AN INCOMING/EXTERNAL FULL BLOCK (P2P + compact + submitblock + mined + repair-rebuild). Callers: msg_blocks.c:324, msg_compact.c:60, miner.c:224 (via process_block_found), mining_controller.c:196, repair_controller_rebuild.c:179. ALL FIVE call the SAME function process_new_block(state, ms, coins_tip, params, pblock, force, datadir), which does (process_block_core.c:1022-1047): (1) check_block stateless, (2) accept_block — header admit + on-disk write + block_index entry, (3) activation_request_connect(SRC_NEW_BLOCK, pblock). REPLACEMENT ENTRY POINT: a single new reducer_ingest_block(pblock, source, &out) that does stateless check_block, then writes the body to disk + admits the header (the accept_block work, see Group-4 gap), then pushes the hash into header_admit_inbox and kicks the staged_sync supervisor. The 5 sites collapse to one call. Note miner.c & mining_controller.c & repair pass force=true; the new entry needs a 'requested/force' arg to skip relay pre-filters (accept_block.c:166-196 uses `requested`).

GROUP 2 — DRIVE A REORG / CHAIN ADVANCE WITH NO NEW BLOCK (pblock=NULL). Callers: boot.c:3230, boot_services.c:1898 (boot catch-up), msg_headers.c:647/706/722 (peer says 'all data present, connect now'), sync_monitor.c:168, utxo_activation_paused.c:77 (Condition auto-heal), repair_controller.c:239, chain_activation_controller.c:181/437 (internal drain). These do NOT carry a block — they ask the engine to walk find_most_work_chain and connect/disconnect to the best tip. REPLACEMENT ENTRY POINT: a reducer_kick()/advance-tick that just wakes the staged_sync supervisor (it already re-reads cursors every tick). For the reducer to honor these, the reducer's tip_finalize stage must itself drive active_chain_set_tip via connect/disconnect — see the gap below.

GROUP 3 — REORG ROLLBACK / INVALIDATE / SELF-HEAL (disconnect_tip + reconnect). Callers: process_block_invalidate.c:229 (invalidateblock — validated disconnect_tip), process_block_self_heal.c:695 (auto-heal disconnect_tip), then process_block_invalidate.c:317/380 + process_block_revalidate.c:384 re-kick activation_request_connect. These reuse the EXISTING validated disconnect_tip and are explicitly marked one-write-path-ok (invalidate-reuses-validated-disconnect). REPLACEMENT: the reducer's utxo_apply_delta.c already has a reorg-unwind path (emit_inverse_delta loop at :731, finality-gated by reorg_is_allowed at :714) and tip_finalize detects reorg (:419 new_tip->pprev != old_tip). The repoint is to make invalidate/reconsider rewind the STAGE CURSOR (header_admit reorg-rewind already exists, header_admit_stage.c:208-255) instead of calling disconnect_tip directly.

GROUP 4 — BOOT / HEADER-ONLY ADMIT (the header path, distinct from full-block). accept_block_header() is called from msg_headers.c:364 (P2P headers), header_probe.c:182/201 (header probe). These create block_index entries WITHOUT bodies and feed activate_best_chain later. The reducer's header_admit + validate_headers stages are the intended replacement, BUT today they only FOLLOW (read active_chain_at), they do not CREATE the index entry from raw header bytes — see the gap below.

CRITICAL GAP #1 — THE REDUCER IS A FOLLOWER, NOT A PRODUCER. header_admit_stage.c:270 reads `active_chain_at(&ms->chain_active, next_h)` and at :271 returns JOB_IDLE if the entry isn't there yet. So the legacy accept_block_header/activate_best_chain MUST run first to populate chain_active. tip_finalize_stage.c:404-406 reads active_chain_at(next_h) and active_chain_at(next_h+1) and returns JOB_IDLE if new_tip is absent (:407). The reducer CANNOT advance past the legacy-set active tip. To DRIVE ingestion the reducer must take over: (a) creating the block_index entry from received header bytes (the add_to_block_index work now in accept_block_header.c, NOT in any stage), and (b) calling active_chain_set_tip (chainstate.c:279) via the connect path — neither happens in any app/jobs/src/*.c stage.

CRITICAL GAP #2 — NO REDUCER STAGE WRITES BLOCK BYTES TO DISK OR QUEUES DOWNLOADS. Verified: grep for write_block_to_disk / find_block_pos / dl_queue / get_download_mgr across all app/jobs/src/*.c returns ZERO hits. body_fetch_stage.c header (lines 5-10) says its step is 'one in-memory flag check + one SQL insert'; body_persist_stage.c header (lines 5-8) says it 'verifies that bodies observed on disk are readable... It is a shadow stage: it writes only body_persist_log'. The on-disk block write (write_block_to_disk, accept_block.c:252) and the find_block_pos allocation are STILL owned exclusively by legacy accept_block. The reducer_ingest_block entry point must absorb this disk-write + the nChainTx-propagation BFS (accept_block.c:281-318).

CRITICAL GAP #3 — THE UTXO AUTHORITY IS A RUNTIME TWO-WRITER GATE, NOT YET FLIPPED. update_coins.c:53 and :77 only emit the shadow projection while utxo_projection_get_author()==UTXO_AUTHOR_LEGACY; the stage (utxo_apply_stage.c:260, utxo_apply_delta.c:730) only emits when ==UTXO_AUTHOR_STAGE. coins_view_stage_backing.c:91 also gates on STAGE. The legacy connect_block STILL does the real SQLite coins write regardless of author. utxo_apply_delta.c:705-711 explicitly states the stage is 'driven AND finality-gated by legacy activate_best_chain' and 'REVISIT when the stage itself drives the live tip'. So even in 'authoritative' utxo mode the legacy connect path runs the actual ingestion; the projection author flag only chooses which side EMITS events, not who CONNECTS.

THE TRUE TIP-WRITE AUTHORITY CHAIN that must move into the reducer: active_chain_set_tip (lib/validation/src/chainstate.c:279) is the only function that mutates the active chain vector + fires g_chain_authority.set_tip (:329-332). It is called ONLY by update_tip (process_block_core.c:840). update_tip is called by connect_tip (connect_tip.c:616) and disconnect_tip (disconnect_tip.c:212). Therefore deleting connect_tip/disconnect_tip/activate_best_chain REQUIRES tip_finalize_stage to become the caller of update_tip/active_chain_set_tip (or an equivalent), executing the connect_block validation (script_validate + proof_validate stages already shadow this) and the coins write inside the stage. The stage cursor (progress.kv) becomes the authoritative tip number.

DRIVER TOPOLOGY: the 8 stages are NOT a single function — each is an independent supervisor child in app/supervisors/src/staged_sync_supervisor.c, registered in pipeline order (header_admit -> validate_headers -> body_fetch -> body_persist -> script_validate -> proof_validate -> utxo_apply -> tip_finalize; comment lines 8-10), each ticked on its own liveness contract (e.g. header_admit_tick at :42 calls header_admit_stage_drain every 2s). The cursors chain via progress.kv (one stage's cursor_out feeds the next's cursor_in floor). A Group-2 'kick' maps to waking these supervisor children, NOT to a synchronous call. This is the existing Job mechanism the repoint targets.

risks: The reducer today CANNOT be made authoritative by a flag flip alone: three stages (header_admit:270, tip_finalize:404, utxo_apply via author gate) READ active_chain_at and never WRITE active_chain_set_tip. Making them drive requires NEW code (capture update_tip/connect_block + disk write + download queue), not just deletion. The task's premise 'Steps 1-9 done' covers MIRRORING (emit events, set HAVE_DATA, read-side projection) — it does NOT cover DRIVE-side capture of active_chain_set_tip, write_block_to_disk, or dl_queue_blocks.

Deleting connect_tip/disconnect_tip also deletes the ONLY callers of update_tip->active_chain_set_tip. If tip_finalize_stage does not first become the caller, the active chain vector is never mutated and the node wedges at boot tip. msg_blocks.c:310-340 has block_mark_seen dedup semantics tightly coupled to whether the block 'made it onto the active chain' (mark-seen post-processing, NOT before, to allow retry on ACTIVATION_SKIP_ALREADY_RUNNING). The reducer is 8 independently-ticked supervisor children on 2s contracts, not a synchronous engine. P2P/mining currently get a synchronous accept/reject (validation_state_is_valid checked inline at msg_blocks.c:327, mining_controller.c:200). utxo_apply_delta.c:700-711 finality depth is measured from the STAGE cursor C-1, explicitly a 'defensive backstop' valid ONLY because legacy activate_best_chain currently finality-gates the active chain. plan.justification:
Pick a HYBRID seam: a synchronous reducer_ingest_block(block, source, force, &verdict) entry that REPLACES the body of activation_request_connect (the one existing chokepoint, chain_activation_controller.c:342, funneling all 9 connect callers), NOT a fully async log-driven model. Justification anchored in real caller needs verified in the traces and my reads:

(1) SYNCHRONOUS VERDICT IS NON-NEGOTIABLE FOR 3 OF 5 INGEST CALLERS. mining_controller.c:196-208 reads `bool ok = process_new_block(...)` then sets the submitblock RPC result string from `format_state_message(&state,...)` — it MUST have an inline accept/reject. miner.c:224 (process_block_found) returns the bool to the mining loop. msg_blocks.c:327-370 branches on `validation_state_is_valid(&state)` inline to (a) decay peer score on good (peer_scoring_on_good_interaction :357), (b) re-request headers on invalid (:346-350), and (c) mark-seen via msg_blocks_should_mark_seen(chain, landed)==active_chain_contains (:259-264, :367) ONLY when the block reached the active chain — a contract that REQUIRES knowing the connect outcome synchronously. A pure-async event_log model (option a) would break all three: submitblock could not return accept/reject, and msg_blocks' retry-vs-dedup ban-scoring contract (the explicit comment at msg_blocks.c:314-320 says do NOT mark seen before connect so SKIP_ALREADY_RUNNING can retry) would have no verdict to key off.

(2) THE CHOKEPOINT ALREADY SERIALIZES. activation_request_connect already takes ctl->mutex (:382), runs activate_best_chain under it (:405), and drains deferred passes in a 2s budget (:420-444). Making the reducer synchronous means: under that SAME mutex, run the 8 stage step bodies inline for the target height(s) instead of calling activate_best_chain, then return the verdict. This preserves the single-writer discipline, the existing async supervisor tickers (staged_sync_supervisor.c:42-52, period 2s) keep running for IBD/catch-up backfill, and the synchronous path just drains the same stage step functions ahead of the tickers when a block arrives. So HYBRID = stages are the engine; the synchronous wrapper drives them for one-block-at-tip and returns accept/reject; the supervisor tickers drive bulk/backfill. This is additive: the wrapper calls the SAME step bodies the tickers already call.

(3) WHY NOT FULLY SYNC-ONLY (no log): the log/cursor (progress.kv + per-stage *_log tables) is already the durable spine (tip_finalize_log is even the non-authoritative fallback for active_chain_height, chainstate.c:352) and gives crash-safe reorg rewind (header_admit_stage.c:208 rewind_cursor_if_active_chain_reorged, utxo_apply_delta.c:737 atomic delete+rewind). Keep it. The verdict is synchronous; the persistence and reorg machinery stay log-driven. Hence hybrid, not pure-(b).

The synchronous reducer_ingest_block, after header_admit places the new block_index and find_most_work_chain selects a candidate whose pprev != current tip, computes fork point and: (1) calls a NEW stage-driven disconnect that, for h = tip down to fork+1, applies the inverse-delta (the machinery already in utxo_apply_delta.c emit_inverse_delta is the source of truth — promote it from "follower re-converge" to "driver" by removing the guard that requires chain_active to already reach C-1, gated instead on reorg_is_allowed(tip,fork) which already exists :714), then (2) rewinds the header_admit/validate/utxo_apply/tip_finalize cursors to fork+1 (header_admit_stage.c:243 stage_set_cursor + utxo_apply_delta.c:753 unwind_write_cursor are the existing primitives), then (3) walks forward connecting fork+1..new_tip through the normal stage step bodies, and (4) the tip-set is performed by the NEW active_chain_set_tip caller in tip_finalize (see must_write). The finality floor (ZCL_FINALITY_DEPTH via reorg_is_allowed) is reused verbatim. Instead add a NEW post-finalize side-effect step owned by tip_finalize (or a 9th "tip_effects" stage child) that runs AFTER tip_finalize records "finalized" (tip_finalize_stage.c:471) and AFTER the stage sets the in-mem tip: for the just-finalized block it (a) reads the block bytes (stage_default_block_reader, stage_helpers.h:58, already used by utxo_apply), (b) calls wallet_sync_transaction + wallet_try_sapling_decrypt + wallet_mark_sapling_nullifiers_spent per tx (lifted verbatim from connect_tip.c:783-818), (c) calls tx_mempool_remove_for_block (connect_tip.c:828), (d) appends MMR/MMB (rpc_blockchain_mmr_append / mmb_leaf, connect_tip.c:860/870). How a reject (bad PoW/Equihash, bad script, bad proof, BIP30) is surfaced. VERIFIED reject producers in the stages: validate_headers_stage runs a multi-threaded g_validator per header (validate_headers_stage.c:113 worker_entry) that does PoW/Equihash and writes ok/fail_reason to validate_headers_log (:222); body_fetch reads that row and on vh_ok==0 records "skipped_invalid" (body_fetch_stage.c:187-197); script_validate/proof_validate stages shadow the ECDSA/Groth16 checks; utxo_apply records "spend_unknown_utxo"/"delta_diverged" (utxo_apply_stage.c:287, :250) and emits EV_BLOCK_REJECTED; tip_finalize emits EV_BLOCK_REJECTED on precondition_failed/utxo_count_diverged (tip_finalize_stage.c:439/461). check_block (stateless PoW+merkle, check_block.c:166/190) runs FIRST in process_new_block (:1022).

DESIGN: reducer_ingest_block keeps the stateless check_block gate inline at the front (cheap PoW/merkle, exactly as process_new_block:1022 does today) so a garbage block is rejected with a verdict BEFORE any stage/log mutation — this gives msg_blocks its DoS/ban verdict and submitblock its immediate "bad-pow" string without polluting the log. For contextual rejects discovered DURING the synchronous stage drain (script/proof/utxo/finalize), the wrapper reads the stage's just-written *_log row (ok=0 + fail_reason) for the target height and maps it into the returned struct validation_state (validation_state_dos/validation_state_error with the fail_reason), so validation_state_is_valid() returns false to msg_blocks.c:327 and the reject_reason string flows to submitblock's format_state_message (mining_controller.c:202). The EV_BLOCK_REJECTED events the stages already emit remain the async/observability channel. Net: stateless rejects are pre-log inline; stateful rejects are read back from the freshly-written log row within the same synchronous call.
